steps.notes: PASS (official joint) with explicit-Euler real-space substep + EXACT exponential k-space propagator exp(dt*(2k^2/q0^2 - k^4/q0^4)), dx=1, n_steps=round(T/dt). Scheme choice is NOT stated and alternatives fail (see findings). Targets encode exact step counts (5,5,10).

PASS (official joint) with Sk = fftshift(|fft2(u)|^2) RAW (no normalization), Kx/Ky = fftshift(2*pi*fftfreq(N,1)) meshgridded with indexing='ij' (Kx varies along axis 0). Normalized variants and meshgrid-default 'xy' labeling fail (see findings).

PASS (official joint) but ONLY after reverse-engineering the radial binning from the h5: histogram with nbins = N//2 over [0, max|k|=sqrt(2)*pi], peak location = bin center, plus a proximity threshold that must accept an 11%-of-q0 deviation. None of these parameters is stated (see findings).

Spec-literal chain (solve_SH to exactly T=50 -> structure_factor -> analyze) FAILS official joint scoring: targets were generated with 9999 steps (T-dt = 49.995), not 10000. Replacing T by T-dt makes all 6 tests PASS. Joint runtime ~60s (well under the official 1800s).

findings.evidence: Prompt: 'The simulation starts from an initial state u0 at time t=0 and stop at a final time T' with T=50., dt=0.005 in all 6 tests; 50/0.005 == 10000.0 EXACTLY in IEEE double, so every natural step count (round(T/dt), int(T/dt), len(np.arange(0,T,dt))) gives 10000 steps. The h5 targets, however, encode 9999 steps: an implementation algorithmically identical to the reference matches target u to maxabs 7.8e-12 with n=9999 but misses by maxabs 6.8e-4 (test 0), 1.1e-4 (t1), 4.7e-4 (t3), 7.9e-4 (t4), 8.5e-4 (t5) with n=10000 -> np.allclose on u FAILS (and Sk misses by up to 5.6e2 absolute) on 5 of 6 tests (test 2 decays to ~1e-13 so both pass). Bit-level perturbation controls (factored vs separate nonlinear update, rfft2 vs fft2) all stay within ~1e-10 of each other after 10000 steps, proving the 6.8e-4 gap is the missing step, not FP-noise amplification. Official runner: steptest 55.4 with solve_SH(u0,dt,T,...) (the same solve_SH that PASSES 55.1) -> 'RESULT step 55.4: FAIL'; with solve_SH(u0,dt,T-dt,...) -> 'RESULT step 55.4: PASS'. Internally inconsistent with 55.1, whose own targets encode the exact counts (5 steps for T=0.05/dt=0.01; 10 steps for T=0.05/dt=0.005, verified to 1.6e-15): no single step-counting rule yields (5, 10, 9999), so a solver reusing their 55.1-passing solver in 55.4 (as the prompt intends) cannot pass both.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the six 55.4 h5 targets with exactly 10000 steps (evolve to t=T), or drop the u and Sk elements from the cmp_tuple_or_list comparison and score only (if_form_stripes, stripe_mode), which are insensitive to the off-by-one.

findings.evidence: Prompt only says 'radially average Sk' and 'When binning is used, use the center value of the bin'; neither the number of bins, the bin range, nor the proximity threshold is stated ('within some reasonable tolerance threshold'). Targets encode nbins = N//2 over [0, kr.max()= sqrt(2)*pi]: test 0 target location 0.9774342463948407 = 5.5*sqrt(2)*pi/25 (N=50), test 1 target 2.221441469079183 = 7.5*sqrt(2)*pi/15 (N=30) - bit-exact bin centers. Since the location is scored with np.allclose (rtol 1e-5), every other natural binning fails: nbins=N gives 1.0219 vs 0.9774 (t0) and 2.1474 vs 2.2214 (t1); fixed nbins=100 gives 0.9996 vs 0.9774 and loses the t1 peak entirely. The proximity threshold is equally load-bearing: t1's peak sits at |2.2214-2| = 0.2214 = 11.1% of q0, so the common 10%-of-q0 tolerance returns (False,0) and FAILS; downstream, 55.4 test 4 (N=200, q0=1) has its peak at 0.95522, |delta| = 0.0448 > one bin width (0.0444), so the also-natural 'within one bin width' tolerance passes all of 55.3 yet fails 55.4 -> any tolerance must lie in a window the solver cannot derive. Additionally the docstring demands a 'narrowness' criterion ('meets combined proximity, narrowness, and height criteria'; peak_widths is imported) but no test constrains it - a solver implementing a strict width cut risks flipping booleans for no spec-backed reason.
findings.suggested_fix: State the recipe numerically in the step prompt/docstring: 'radially average Sk with np.histogram using N//2 bins over [0, max|k|]; report the bin center; a peak counts as near q0 if |k_peak - q0| <= 0.5*q0 (e.g.); no width criterion is applied'.

findings.evidence: Background only says: 'we tranform the tranport term -[2q0^-2 nabla^2 + q0^-4 nabla^4]u to k-space, and update it in k-space based on u1' - no time-integration rule for the k-space substep is given. The targets encode the EXACT exponential propagator exp(dt*(2k^2/q0^2 - k^4/q0^4)) (matches test 2 to 2.3e-14 relative). The semi-implicit Euler factor 1/(1-dt*L) - the standard scheme in the Swift-Hohenberg literature - differs by max 4.7% relative on test 2 (k_max=pi, dt*L ~ 1 is NOT small), and explicit Euler (1+dt*L) by 5.4%: both FAIL np.allclose. A solver must guess 'exact exponential' from the phrase 'split-step'; the real-space substep is likewise unstated but explicit Euler (u1 = u + dt*(eps*u - u - u^3)) matches the uniform-field test 1 value 0.9390147345933418 exactly and is the only natural choice there.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the step background: 'integrate the linear transport substep exactly in k-space, i.e. multiply each Fourier mode by exp(dt*(2k^2/q0^2 - k^4/q0^4)); use one explicit-Euler step for the local term'.

findings.evidence: Background defines 'S(k,t) = |U(k,t)|^2 where U(k,t) denotes the Fourier component of u' with no normalization stated. The target is the RAW numpy transform: fftshift(|fft2(u)|^2) (test 0 max 33366.63 matches |fft2|^2 max bit-exactly). Reading 'Fourier component' as the coefficient in u = sum_k U_k e^{ikx} (i.e. fft2/N^2, standard in physics) gives values N^4 = 1.6e5 times smaller, and the per-site convention |fft2|^2/N^2 is also common; both verified to FAIL np.allclose against the target. min_height=1e-12 downstream gives no magnitude cue.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify in the docstring: 'Sk = |np.fft.fft2(u)|^2 with no normalization, fftshift-ed so k=0 is centered'.

findings.evidence: Docstring says 'Kx: coordinates in k space conjugate to x' but never states which array axis of the N*N array u is x. The target has Kx varying along axis 0 (rows): target Kx[:,0] = [-3.142, -2.827, ...] while Kx[0,:] is constant, i.e. np.meshgrid(k, k, indexing='ij'). A solver using numpy's meshgrid DEFAULT indexing='xy' produces exactly the transposed labeling (verified: xy-Kx == target Ky bit-exactly) and fails the tuple np.allclose, even though their Sk is identical. Nothing in the prompt or test construction (u = np.tile(np.sin(np.arange(N)),(N,1)) varies along axis 1, which the target labels as y) lets the solver determine the mapping.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the docstring: 'the first array index corresponds to x (Kx varies along axis 0), e.g. Kx, Ky = np.meshgrid(k, k, indexing="ij")'.

findings.evidence: Test 0 (u0 = np.zeros, target all-zeros, since u=0 is a fixed point) is passed by any zero-preserving function including the trivial 'return u'. No score impact because tests 1-2 constrain the dynamics and joint scoring requires all three.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace test 0 with a non-trivial initial condition, or keep as a smoke test (cosmetic).

findings.evidence: Test 2 (epsilon=-0.5) decays to |u|max ~ 3.9e-13, so the frozen tuple is effectively (0-field, 0-field, False, 0): a trivial implementation returning (np.zeros((N,N)), np.zeros((N,N)), False, 0) passes this entire test under cmp_tuple_or_list (atol=1e-8). No score impact alone since the other five tests constrain; it is also the only 55.4 test immune to the 9999-step off-by-one.
findings.suggested_fix: None required; optionally shorten T for the decaying case so the target is not numerically degenerate.

overall_assessment: Steps 55.1-55.3 are solvable but each hinges on at least one unstated convention (exact-exponential k-space propagator; raw-|fft2|^2 structure factor with 'ij' axis labeling; an N//2-bin radial histogram and a proximity threshold that must sit in a narrow unstatable window) - a competent solver passes only by guessing the authors' choices, since plausible standard alternatives miss the frozen targets by far more than np.allclose tolerance. Step 55.4 is a confirmed blocker: its six targets were generated with 9999 time steps instead of the 10000 the prompt's T=50/dt=0.005 demands (verified by bit-level reproduction at 8e-12 with n=9999 and official steptest PASS only when evolving to T-dt), so a solver whose solve_SH correctly passes 55.1 deterministically fails 55.4. The problem is not fair to score as-is; regenerating the 55.4 targets at exactly T and pinning the analysis conventions in the prompts would fix it.
